Analyses the recordings with BirdNET

Source: R/birdnet.R
analyze_birdnet.Rd

Uses the BirdNET v2.4 model through the birdnetR package.

Usage

analyze_birdnet(
  am,
  min_confidence = 0.1,
  language = default_language(),
  version = "v2.4",
  location_filter = TRUE,
  location_threshold = 0.03,
  species_list = NULL,
  overlap = 0,
  sensitivity = 1,
  threads = NULL,
  reanalyze = FALSE,
  stop_on_error = FALSE
)

Arguments

am

Object created with read_audiomoth().

min_confidence

Minimum confidence (0-1) of the detections that are kept. Values below 0.1 make the cache keep more detections (a new analysis).

language

Language of the common names. By default, the language of the operating system (see check_requirements()); codes such as "es", "en_us", "en_uk", "fr", "de", "pt"... Polish ("pl") is not accepted: its label file in BirdNET v2.4 is wrong.

version

Version of the BirdNET model (see birdnetR::birdnet_model_tflite()). It is stored in the column model and quoted by export_observation() in the notes.

location_filter

Filter the species by location and week (see "Which species BirdNET looks for"). Not applied when species_list is given.

location_threshold

Minimum probability of occurrence (metadata model, 0 to 1) for a species to pass the location filter.

species_list

Own list of the species to look for, instead of the location filter: a vector of scientific names, the path of a .txt file (e.g. the species list of BirdNET-Analyzer) or of a .csv file, or a data frame such as the result of gbif_species_list(). See read_species_list(). NULL (default): no list.

overlap

Overlap between 3 s windows (seconds, 0 to 2.9).

sensitivity

BirdNET sensitivity (0.5 to 1.5).

threads

Computing threads (by default, all but one).

reanalyze

Analyse every recording again with these parameters.

stop_on_error

Stop with an error when BirdNET cannot analyse some recording (useful in scripts run with Rscript); by default it only warns, and the recordings are listed in the column analysis.

Value

am with am$detections (data frame).

Details

Which species BirdNET looks for. BirdNET v2.4 knows about 6,500 classes, most of them birds from all over the world. Without a filter it often proposes species from other continents, so by default only the species expected at the site are considered:

  • Location filter (default, location_filter = TRUE): the metadata (geographic) model of BirdNET, trained with the eBird checklists, gives for each species a probability of occurrence at the location of the deployment and in the week of the year of each recording (48 weeks, four per month). Only the species with a probability of at least location_threshold (0.03, the value of BirdNET) are analysed; the others are never proposed. It works well for common species, but in little visited areas, or for species that are seldom reported to eBird (nocturnal, secretive or scarce species: owls, Stone-curlew, sandgrouse...), the probability may be underestimated and the species left out. In such cases lower location_threshold (e.g. 0.01), use a species_list or turn the filter off.

  • Own list (species_list): only the species of the list are analysed, wherever the recorder is (the location filter is then not applied). It may be a vector of scientific names, a file such as the species list of BirdNET-Analyzer or a CSV file, or a table built from the observations around the site with gbif_species_list(); see read_species_list() for the accepted formats.

  • No filter (location_filter = FALSE): all the classes of BirdNET. Rare species are not lost, but there are more mistakes with species from elsewhere: check the records by ear (create_validation()).

In every case the probability of occurrence of the metadata model is kept in the column location_prob of the detections, and the validation page shows first the least plausible records (low confidence and low location_prob).

Cache. Recordings already analysed with the same parameters are not analysed again: an interrupted analysis continues where it stopped. The cache is in <output>/birdnet/, in one folder per combination of parameters, so going back to earlier parameters reuses their results. Changing min_confidence (above 0.1) or language does not require a new analysis.

Doubts. BirdNET analyses the audio in 3 s windows. A detection has "no doubts" (no_doubts = TRUE) when BirdNET proposed no other species in the same window with a confidence of at least 0.1 (only species that pass the location filter, or that are in the species_list, count; classes such as "Engine" or "Human vocal" do not).

Overlap. With overlap > 0 consecutive windows overlap and the same song is detected in several of them. The column event groups the overlapping windows of the same species, and the counts of species_summary() and export_observation() use events, not windows.

At the end, AudioMoth_<ID>_detections.csv is saved (see read_detections()) and am$recordings gains the column analysis ("ok", "error: ..." or NA for recordings that are not valid).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Not run: the first time it installs Python, TensorFlow and the BirdNET
# model (about 3 GB, a few minutes)
card <- system.file("extdata", "example", "card", package = "AudiomothR")
am <- read_audiomoth(card, coordinates = "41.00, -3.00", output = tempfile())
am <- analyze_birdnet(am)

# Only the species of an own list (e.g. that of BirdNET-Analyzer)
am <- analyze_birdnet(am, species_list = "~/species_list.txt")

# The species observed within 30 km in GBIF (eBird, Observation.org, iNaturalist)
am <- analyze_birdnet(am, species_list = gbif_species_list(am, radius_km = 30))
} # }
